en: Catalog number: M00570 Uniform title: *Siddhilakṣmīmantroddhara*

Manuscript: NGMCP manuscript no. 5-848, Reel no. B 28/23 Description: Ritual manual Notes: Manuscript selected by Dr. Mark S.G. Dyczkowski. Data-entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Dr. Anirban Dash. Revision 0: October 3, 2021.

I worship Mṛtyuñjaya, whose limbs are as pure and white as camphor, who bestows auspiciousness upon those whose bodies are closely joined to his own, and whose radiant crown is embraced by the surging waves of the Gaṅgā.
Now, the manual for the daily worship of the illustrious Mṛtyuñjaya, together with the four sanctuaries beginning with Śrī Gaṇapati and their constituent limbs,
is being written.

Therein, first, the worshipper, having performed his daily obligatory rites, should offer water for the guest-offering (*argha*) to the Sun: *Oṃ haṃ saḥ, obeisance to this guest-offering for the purpose of performing the five-shrine worship (*pañcāyatana-pūjā*) to the venerable Lord Śrī Sūrya.*
One should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) and breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the root mantra. Having formed the *añjali* gesture:

"Of this venerable Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, Kahola is the seer (*ṛṣi*), the Gāyatrī meter is the metre (*chanda*), Mṛtyuñjaya is the deity (*devatā*); its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of longevity, health, and desired success. *Oṃ*, salutation to Kahola the seer; [place] on the head.
Oṃ, obeisance to the goddess Gāyatrī, the meter; [place this] on the mouth.
Oṃ, salutation to the deity Mṛtyuñjaya; [placed] at the heart. Salutation for the attainment of longevity, health, and desired goals.

The ritual assignment of limbs (karāṅganyāsa): SĀṂ, salutation to the heart; SĪṂ, svāhā to the head; SŪṂ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair; SAĪṂ, hūṃ to the armor; SAUṂ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; SAḤ, phaṭ to the weapon. Thus for the eight [limbs], beginning with the heart.

The Installation of the Arghya Vessel: *Raṃ*, salutation to the fire-maṇḍala; *Haṃ*, salutation to the sun-maṇḍala; *Saṃ*, salutation to the moon-maṇḍala. Having worshipped with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should sprinkle oneself and the articles of worship with that very water.
The worship of the seat: Oṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti. Oṃ, obeisance to Ananta.
Oṃ, homage to the bulbous root. Oṃ, homage to the stalk. Oṃ, homage to the lotus. Oṃ, homage to the petals.
Oṃ, homage to the filaments. Oṃ, homage to the pericarp.
Then, the worship of the pīṭha-śaktis.
Oṃ, obeisance to Vāmā. Oṃ, obeisance to Jyeṣṭhā. Oṃ, obeisance to Raudrī. Oṃ, obeisance to Kālī.
Oṃ, obeisance to Kalavikaraṇī. Oṃ, obeisance to Balavikaraṇī. Oṃ, obeisance to Balapramathinī.

Oṃ, homage to the Subduer of All Beings. Oṃ, homage to Manonmanī. Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Infinite One, who is endowed with the power whose essence is all qualities, the self-nature of the Yoga-seat.

Then one should worship Gaṇeśa. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): For this one-syllable mantra of Gaṇapati, the seer is Gaṇaka, the metre is *nivṛt*, and the deity is Gaṇapati; its application (*viniyoga*) is for the attainment of desired goals.

On the head: *namaḥ* to the sage Gaṇaka. On the mouth: *namaḥ* to the Nivṛt-chandas. On the heart: *namaḥ* to the deity Śrī-Vighna. *Gāṃ* to the heart, *namaḥ*. *Gīṃ* to the head, *svāhā*. *Gūṃ* to the crest-lock (*śikhā*), *vaṣaṭ*. *Gaiṃ* to the armor (*kavaca*), *hūṃ*. *Gauṃ* to the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*. *Gaḥ* to the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*. Thus.

[The worship] of the heart and so forth: "To Ādhāraśakti," and so on (8). [This is] the worship of the pedestal (*pīṭhapūjana*). Oṃ, salutation to Tīvrā. Oṃ, salutation to Jvālinī. Oṃ, salutation to Nandā. Oṃ, salutation to Bhogadā. Oṃ, salutation to Kāmarūpiṇī. Oṃ, salutation to Ugrā. Oṃ, salutation to Tejovatī. Oṃ, salutation to Satyā. In the center: Oṃ, salutation to Vighnanāśinī. Oṃ, salutation to Sarvaśakti.
Salutation to the one whose seat is the lotus.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).

Having the luster of vermilion, three eyes, and broad, prominent tusks; holding in his lotus-like hands a tusk, a noose, a goad, and the gesture of granting boons; beautiful with a shining citron fruit upon his massive trunk; with a crown resplendent with the crescent moon, an elephantine face, and temples flowing with ichor like the rising half-moon.
O lords of serpents, worship Gaṇapati, who is adorned with ornaments and possesses divine garments and unguents.

Having meditated thus, one should worship with the ritual services beginning with water for the feet (*pādya*). [With] three handfuls of offerings (*tryañjali*): *Gaṃ, obeisance to Gaṇapati*. [Performing] the six-limbed rite (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*): *Oṃ, twice, to the long-trunked one; Oṃ, twice, to the single-tusked one; Oṃ, twice, to the large-bellied one; Oṃ, twice, to the elephant-faced one; Oṃ, twice, to the long-bellied one; Oṃ, twice, to the formidable one.* Oṃ... [and so on].
Salutation to Vighnarāja. Oṃ, salutation to the smoke-colored one (twice). [Offerings] from incense, lamp, and food oblation (naivedya) up to the recitation (japa).
p. 3b) Gaṃ 10 || Praise ||
He who is worshipped by the supreme gods for the sake of accomplishing their desired aims.
Salutation to that Lord of the Gaṇas, the destroyer of all obstacles.
Then one should worship the Sun.
Of this Śrīsūryayama mantra, Manu is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas), Sūryaya is the deity (devatā),
and the application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining the accomplishment of unseen fruits.
Salutation to the sage Manu at the head; salutation to the Gāyatrī meter at the mouth; salutation to the deity Sūrya at the heart.
The ritual placement (nyāsa): Hrāṃ, salutation to the heart; Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head; Hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Hraiṃ, for the armor, hūṃ. Hrauṃ, for the three eyes, vauṣaṭ. Hraḥ, for the weapon, phaṭ.
With this [mantra], one worships the heart and other [limbs] (6). With "Oṃ, to Ādhāraśakti," and so forth (8), one should worship the pedestal: Oṃ, salutation to Dīptā;
Oṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmā, twice (2).

Oṃ, homage to Jayā. Oṃ, homage to Bhadrā. Oṃ, homage to Vibhūti. Oṃ, homage to Vimalā. Oṃ, homage to Amoghā. Oṃ, homage to Vidyutā. Oṃ, homage to Sarvatomukhī. In the center: Oṃ, homage to the Solar Seat (saurapīṭha), whose nature consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva.
Meditative concentration.

I worship the Sun, who sits upon a seat of red lotuses, the unique ocean of all virtues, the sovereign of all worlds, holding two lotuses, the gesture of fearlessness, and the gesture of granting boons in his lotus-like hands.
[He who bears] a crest of rubies, whose bodily luster is crimson, and who possesses three eyes.
Having meditated thus, one should worship with the ritual services beginning with water for the feet (pādya). [This is done] with three handfuls of offerings (tryañjali).
Hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, salutation to Sūrya (3). [This is] the six-limbed [mantra]. One should worship the enclosure.
Sāṃ, obeisance to Soma. Aṃ, obeisance to Aṅgāra. Vuṃ, obeisance to Budha.

vṛṃ to Bṛhaspati, twice. śuṃ to Śukra, twice. śaṃ to Śanaiścara, twice. rāṃ to Rāhu, twice. keṃ to Ketu, twice. [Offerings] ending with incense, lamp, and food oblation (naivedya). Japa: hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, ten times.
Praise.
Salutation to Savitṛ, the sole eye of the universe, the cause of the origin, maintenance, and destruction of the world;
who consists of the three Vedas, who assumes the nature of the three *guṇas*, and whose essence is Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa, and Śaṅkara.
Then one should worship Viṣṇu.
Of this twelve-syllable mantra, Prajāpati is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandas),
Viṣṇu is the deity (devatā), and its application (viniyoga) is for the attainment of the fruits of the four aims of human life.

On the head: Oṃ, salutation to Prajāpati, the Seer (Ṛṣi). On the mouth: salutation to Gāyatrī, the Metre (Chandas). On the heart: salutation to Viṣṇu, the Deity (Devatā). This is the ritual placement (Nyāsa).
Oṃ, homage to the heart; Svāhā, homage to the head; Vaṣaṭ, to the Blessed One, the crest-lock.
Oṃ Vāsudevāya kavacāya huṃ. Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya astrāya phaṭ.
By this [mantra], the five-limbed assignment (pañcāṅganyāsa) beginning with the heart is performed. [Then] one should worship the pedestal (pīṭha) with "Oṃ Ādhāraśaktaye," and so forth:
Oṃ, salutation to Vimalā; Oṃ, salutation to Utkarṣiṇī; Oṃ, salutation to Jñānā; Oṃ, salutation to Kriyā; Oṃ, salutation to Yogā.
Oṃ to Prahvī, twice. Oṃ to Satyā, twice. Oṃ to Īśānā, twice. In the center, salutation to Anugrahā.
Oṃ, salutation to Vāsudeva, the self of all beings, the seat of the yoga-throne of all.
Meditative absorption.
Hari, whose arms are like iron bars bearing a radiant discus, lotus, and mace, is seated upon a white lotus.
I always bow down to him who wears bracelets, armlets, necklaces, and a crown, and who possesses the luster of fresh jasmine.

With three joined palms (*tryañjali*): *Namo bhagavate vāsudevāya*. (3) With the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*). *Oṃ vāsudevāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ pradyumnāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ aniruddhāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ śāntyai namaḥ*. *Oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ*. *Oṃ śriyai namaḥ*. *Oṃ ratyai namaḥ*. *Oṃ...*

To Śaṅkha, twice. Oṃ, to Cakra, twice. Oṃ, to Gadā, twice. Oṃ, to Padma, twice. Oṃ, to Kaustubha, twice. Oṃ, to Khaḍga, twice. Oṃ, to Vanamālā, twice. Oṃ, to Garuḍa, twice. Oṃ, to Dhvaja, twice. Oṃ, to Aruṇa, twice. Oṃ, to Durgā, twice. Oṃ, to Īśvara, twice. Oṃ, obeisance to Candra. [Perform the rites] ending with incense, lamp, and food offering (naivedya).
By means of the root-mantra, ten [times].
p. 6a) Praise.
Victory to you, O lotus-eyed one; salutations to you, O creator of the universe!
Salutations to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, the primordial source of the Great Puruṣa.
Then one should worship Durgā: "Of this eight-syllabled Śrī Durgā mantra, Nārada is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chandas*), and Śrī Durgā is the deity (*devatā*);
its application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of accomplishing all my desired goals."
Salutation to the sage Nārada on the head. Salutation to the metre Gāyatrī in the mouth. Salutation to the deity Śrī Durgā in the heart. [This is] the Nyāsa.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, salutation to the heart of Durgā, hrīṃ.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, to Durgā, hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, vaṣaṭ to Durgā, to Hrīṃ, and to Śikhā.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, for Durgā; hrīṃ, for the armor; hūṃ.
Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, to Durgā, hrīṃ, for the three eyes, vauṣaṭ.

Oṃ hrīṃ duṃ, obeisance to Durgā; hrīṃ, phaṭ to the weapon (astra). With this [mantra], one should worship the heart and the other [limbs] (hṛdayādi) six times. Then, one should worship the pedestal (pīṭha), beginning with "Obeisance to Ādhāraśakti" and so forth: Oṃ āṃ, obeisance to Prabhā; īṃ, obeisance to Māyā; ūṃ, obeisance to Jayā; eṃ, obeisance to Sūkṣmā.

Aiṃ, salutation to Viśuddhā (twice). Oṃ, salutation to Nandinī (twice). Auṃ, salutation to Suprabhā (twice). Aṃ, salutation to Vijayā (twice). Aḥ, salutation to Sarvasiddhā. In the center: Oṃ, salutation to the Great Lion whose weapons are adamantine claws and fangs, Hūṃ Phaṭ! Namaḥ.
Meditative absorption.
Seated upon a lion, crowned with the moon, resembling a young elephant, and adorned with three eyes, she holds a conch, a discus, a bow, and arrows in her four arms; she is graced by armlets,
necklaces, bracelets, jingling girdles, and tinkling anklets.
May she who removes difficult states of existence be present, adorned with earrings shimmering with jewels.
Having meditated thus, one should worship with the ritual services beginning with the water for the feet (pādya).
p. 7a) With three *añjali*s: *oṃ hrīṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ* (three times). The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). One should worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*):

*jaṃ jayāyai namaḥ*; *viṃ vijayāyai* (twice); *kīṃ kīrtyai* (twice); *prīṃ prītyai* (twice); *praṃ prabhāyai* (twice); *śraṃ śraddhāyai* (twice); *meṃ medhāyai* (twice); *śruṃ śrutyai* (twice); *śaṃ*.
Śaṃ to the conch, twice; Caṃ to the discus, twice; Gaṃ to the mace, twice; Khaṃ to the sword, twice; Pāṃ to the noose, twice.
Aṃ, twice, to the goad; Śaṃ, twice, to the arrows; Dhaṃ, twice, to the bow. [Offer] incense, lamps, and food offerings, ending with the naivedya.
Recite the root mantra ten times.
Praise.
O most auspicious among all that is auspicious, O Śivā, who accomplishes all purposes,
O refuge, O Tryambikā, O Gaurī, O Nārāyaṇī, salutations be to you!
Furthermore, having performed breath control (prāṇāyāma) and the six-limbed ritual placement (ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa), one should meditate.
With eyes like the sun and moon and a smiling face, he stands between two lotuses;

his hands hold the mudrā, a noose, a deer, and a rosary; he possesses the radiance of cool rays, his body is bathed in the nectar of millions of moons, and he shines brilliantly adorned with necklaces and other ornaments.
I worship Bhava, the Lord of Creatures (Paśupati), the conqueror of death, who deludes the entire universe with his splendor.

Having meditated thus, one should worship with the root mantra using water for the feet (*pādya*) and other offerings, and then worship the enclosure (*āvaraṇa*). One should worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*):
*oṃ anantāya namaḥ*; *oṃ sūkṣmāya namaḥ*; *oṃ śivottamāya namaḥ*; *oṃ ekanetrāya namaḥ*; *oṃ ekarudrāya namaḥ*; *oṃ trimūrtaye namaḥ*; *oṃ śrīkaṇṭhāya namaḥ*; *oṃ śikhaṇḍine namaḥ*. *Oṃ...*
To Umā, twice. Oṃ, to Caṇḍeśvara, twice. Oṃ, to Nandin, twice. Oṃ, to Mahākāla, twice. Oṃ, to Gaṇeśa, twice.
Oṃ, to Vṛṣabha, twice.
Oṃ bhṛṅgine 2 || Oṃ skandāya 2 || Oṃ, homage to Indra and the other guardians of the world (lokapālas).
Oṃ, homage to the primordial vajra weapons! Having offered incense, lamps, food offerings, and betel leaf.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to Mṛtyuñjaya. One should perform the *ārātrika* rite.
O Śambhu, accept this *ārātrika*—the radiance of the fire, the sun, the moon, and the planets—for my accomplishment. Oṃ.
Recitation with the root mantra: 54 times. Praise.

If even the hymn of Brahmā and others is inadequate as praise for You, whose greatness is beyond the furthest limit, then all speech fails before You; yet, O Śarva, You are not inexpressible when one praises You according to the reach of one's own intellect.
This assembly of mine is also faultless in its praise of Hara.

One should perform the praise beginning with these words. Having performed the mouth-instrument, prostrations with the staff-like body, and so forth, one should dwell in happiness. May there be auspiciousness!

Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One Vāsudeva. Yudhiṣṭhira said: [The forms] consisting of the fish, the lotus, the yellow mark, the *liṅga*, the womb, the trident, the rosary, the *iṣṭā* (wished-for), the *abhaya* (fearlessness), and the deer; as well as the *khaṭvāṅga*, that which is called the quiver, the hand-drum (*ḍamaru*), and the feet of Śiva.
